feedback: Frank's confession follows directly from the installed-versus-approved barrier contradiction and his earlier admitted visit to the waiting glass. It confirms that he accessed the bottle during the preview and used its contents later, which supplies exact actions inferred rather than witnessed before voting; these do not replace the already available decisive contradiction. The drawing-versus-room language fits an architect whose reputation depends on promises and safety, although its repetition sounds slightly polished for a spontaneous confession. Brie and Hugh receive credible consequences rather than total moral absolution. The ending feels earned and emotionally satisfying, with the same small evidentiary limitation that opportunity was shared until Frank's false claim singled him out.
